source: Struware CS2024, Ver 2024-03-08 (www.struware.com) - a commercial ASCE 7-16 implementation by a third party
report: Struware published example calculation set, 'Wind Loads - Components & Cladding', sheet 10 of 34, with the GCp table that produced it on sheet 11
basis: Wind Loads : ASCE 7-16, IBC 2021 (printed on sheet 2 of the same set)
status: complete - inputs and outputs both recorded, the run is reproducible from this file alone

READ_THIS_FIRST.which_procedure: The sheet is headed 'Components & Cladding : Alternate design 60'<h<90''. Struware's building is h = 62 ft, so it is ABOVE the 60 ft limit of Chapter 30 Part 1 and takes the alternate route.
READ_THIS_FIRST.why_it_still_verifies_part_1: The GCp values Struware prints ARE the Fig. 30.3-1 and Fig. 30.3-2A values - they reproduce the published figures' endpoints exactly, and the alternate procedure's whole point is that it re-uses those figures. So the run verifies THE TABLES AND THE INTERPOLATION, which is what this package implements.
READ_THIS_FIRST.what_it_therefore_does_NOT_verify: Anything specific to the h <= 60 ft route that is not the GCp figures themselves. If the alternate procedure applies some factor that happens to be 1.0 at these inputs, this run could not see it. The package restricts itself to h <= 60 ft buildings, where Part 1 applies directly.
READ_THIS_FIRST.pdf_extraction_note: In the extracted text the roof GCp table appears under a heading about elevated buildings from ASCE 7-22. That is a text-layer artefact: those GCp values multiply through Eq. 30.3-1 to give sheet 10's roof pressures EXACTLY, at all eight areas and all five rows, which is how their identity was established rather than assumed.

roof_fig_30_3_2A.comment: GCp printed at 10/100/500/1000 ft2; pressures printed at 10/20/50/100/200/350/500/1000 ft2.

breakpoints_this_implies.1': flat at -0.9 to 100 ft2, then log-linear to -0.4 at 1000 ft2
breakpoints_this_implies.1: -1.7 at 10 ft2 to -1.0 at 500 ft2, flat beyond
breakpoints_this_implies.2: -2.3 at 10 ft2 to -1.4 at 500 ft2, flat beyond
breakpoints_this_implies.3: -3.2 at 10 ft2 to -1.4 at 500 ft2, flat beyond
breakpoints_this_implies.+: +0.3 at 10 ft2 to +0.2 at 100 ft2, flat beyond

wall_fig_30_3_1.comment: Struware prints (GCp - GCpi) here, NOT GCp alone - the column is headed 'Walls GCp +/- GCpi'. The raw GCp is recovered by adding back GCpi.
wall_fig_30_3_1.footnote_printed_by_struware: Note: GCp reduced by 10% due to roof angle <= 10 deg.

breakpoints_this_implies.then: all three multiplied by 0.90 for theta <= 10 deg

minimum_cc_pressure.clause: ASCE 7-16 Sect. 30.2.2 - not less than a net 16 lb/ft2 acting in EITHER direction normal to the surface
minimum_cc_pressure.where_it_is_visible: The positive-roof row reads 17.20, 16.10, 16.00, 16.00, 16.0, 16.0, 16.0, 16.0. The first two are computed (17.21 and 16.13 longhand); every later one is the floor, because GCp has fallen to +0.20 and qh(0.20+0.18) = 13.6 psf.
minimum_cc_pressure.negative_control: The floor must NOT touch the suction rows, and it does not - the smallest of them is -20.8 psf, comfortably past 16.

flags_this_can_close: cladding.log_interpolation - the 100 and 200 ft2 columns are interior points, so they test the interpolation and not only the endpoints
cladding.theta_10_deg_wall_reduction - the wall values only reproduce with the 0.9 factor applied
cladding.minimum_cc_pressure - visible in the positive-roof row, with a free negative control on the suction rows
flags_this_cannot_close: cladding.effective_wind_area - Struware tabulates against area as an INPUT, so it never exercises Sect. 26.2's span/3 rule. Closed instead by longhand arithmetic on both branches.
